title: headless_cli private_workspace: surface a refused stable workspace on /loa, WARN once with the path, consider quarantine instead of refusal; a default ACL must not count as an access ACL
description: Bridgebuilder PR #1274 BB-002 + BB-007 (claude-headless voice, DISPUTED): private_workspace() raises EEXIST when the stable per-CLI directory has any entry and complete() turns that into ProviderUnavailableError, so one stray file written by a CLI into its cwd disables every later hop of that provider with no /loa visibility and only a remove-it message; a default ACL (setfacl -d) is treated as an access ACL and refuses the directory. Fail-closed is by design (cycle-126 sprint-247/248); add visibility (loa-status provider line, one WARNING with the exact path) and consider quarantining unexpected entries to <base>/<name>.quarantine/<ts>/ so a voice is never silently lost; distinguish default from access ACL entries.

title: Ablation containers: hold the codex credential outside the agent-writable HOME (host-side proxy or sidecar for the dissent voice) — audit DISS-C-001 of Sprint 261
description: pipeline-run.sh make_home() copies ~/.codex/auth.json (access_token, id_token, account_id — all required by the codex CLI, verified on the host: a copy without id_token gets 401 Missing bearer) into <run>/meta/home/.codex, bind-mounted read-write at /home/evaluser where the agent under evaluation runs with Bash and network. The refresh token is a placeholder (KF-048) and the access token is bounded by the pre-flight horizon, but the agent can read the bearer for the token's lifetime (10 days observed). Accepted for cycle-130 as a documented exposure (the agent is Opus under the harness's own prompts; the token is a ChatGPT-plan token). Design for the next cycle: a host-side proxy or sidecar that holds the credential and exposes only an authenticated local endpoint to the codex process, or a short-lived scoped token minted per run.
